newsitem.title: USA: Detroit Ed sees Fermi nuke restart this wk.
newsitem.headline: Detroit Ed sees Fermi nuke restart this wk.

text.p: Detroit Edison's 1,116 megawatt Fermi 2 nuclear power unit, which automatically shut down Saturday, was expected to restart "in the next day or two," a company spokeswoman said Monday.

"It was a malfunction in the backfill system, related to plant instrumentation," she said, noting the water level in the reactor was not high as reported earlier by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC).
The unit, in Newport, Mich., will likely synchronize to the grid in several days, she said.
Detroit Edison, which owns and operates Fermi 2, is a subsidiary of DTE Energy Corp.
